Tabarak Hossain with Urmee Rahman, Advocates—For the Petitioners 
Sudipta Arjun with Chanchal Kumar Biswas, Advocates—For the Opposite-Parties
parties:
Sultan (Md.) and another ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Attar Ali and others ----- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioners obtained leave challenging legality and propriety of the judgment and order dated 28-3-2011 passed by the learned District Judge, Moulvi bazar, in Civil Revision No. 16 of 2009. Point of law involves herein whether present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction is barred by res-judicata and limitation in view of the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 for permanent injunction filed by the plaintiff-opposite party impleading petitioners herein as defendants for the self-same property. Both the courts below arrived at a negative finding. 

 7. Mr. Tabarak Hossain, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the former suit for permanent injunction between the same parties over the selfsame property was finally decided by a competent court vide judgment and decree dated 19-4-2005 and, as such, present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 is barred by res-judicata. He also submits that the court below committed an illegality in not holding that the cause of action as stated in the former suit was 15-11-1999 as such, present suit for declaration after 9(nine) years from the date of cause of action is clearly barred by limitation. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Abdul Malek Sawdagar vs Md. Mahbubey Alam, reported in 57 DLR (AD) 19 and the case of Hafizuddin Sarker and Lakjan Bewa being dead their heirs: Nur Hossain vs Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 57. 

 8. On the other hand Mr. Sudipta Arjun, learned advocate for the opposite party No. 1 by filing a counter affidavit submits that the issue of the formar suit and present suit are distinct and separate as such, court below rightly and justly passed the impugned judgment and order. He also submits that the plea of res-judicata can be resolved at the trial after framing an issue and cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint. He further submits that the question of limitation is a mixed question of law and fact which can be decided only after taking evidence as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Md. Danesh vs Md. Kala Meah, reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 275, the case of Rawshan Jamil vs Md. Adiluzzaman, reported in 19 BLC (AD) 129 and the case of Shahabuddin (Md.) vs Habibur Rahman, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 99. 

 10. Admittedly, opposite party No. 1 here-in as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 for permanent injunction impleading the petitioners herein along with others as defendants over the selfsame suit land. The suit was dismissed vide judgment and decree dated 30-8-2000 against which plaintiff as appellant preferred appeal in the court of learned District Judge who after hearing the parties allowed the appeal and send back the suit on remand for retrial. It is also admitted that after remand, plaintiff failed to pursue his cause in the trial court which is admitted by the plaintiff in paragraph No. 5 of the plaint of present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 but question remains whether present suit i.e. Title Suit No. 108 of 2008 for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction is barred by res-judicata in view of the judgment arid decree passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 filed by the same plaintiff for dispute over the self same property against same set of defendants seeking permanent injunction. It is already settled by our apex court that Order VII, rule 11 clause (d) is not available for rejection of plaint under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure inasmuch as the plea of res-judicata as contained in section 11 of the Code can be resolved at the trial after framing an issue and cannot be decided from a mere reading of the plaint. It is also settled that the question of limitation being a mixed question of law and fact should be decided only at the trial after taking evidence. Formar suit i.e. Title Suit No. 59 of 1999 filed by the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff for permanent injunction and the present suit filed by the self-same plaintiff for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction. So, it cannot be said that the issues decided in the former suit are same in the present suit. It appears from the averments of the plaint that the plaintiff failed to pursue his cause in the former suit when the same was send back on remand for retrial for his personal difficulties. Whether there was willful negligency of the plaintiff in pursuing his cause in the former suit after sent back on remand or the plea taken in the plaint is genuine is also matter of evidence. In such view of the matter, I do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of the appellate court below.
